correctness.rationale: For every doubleton cell, fixing an action of the unique duplicated type if there is at most one duplicated type leaves only one joint profile for its two required outcomes, proving necessity. With two duplicated types, parity of their indices realizes both cell outcomes on every fixed-agent slice, and partition disjointness isolates the cells; this constructs all feasible vectors. The doubled-type set meets every triangle edge iff at least two of its vertices are selected, so it is exactly a vertex cover; giving 2 copies on a minimum cover yields N+tau(H) and no optimum can use more than 2 copies at any type. The proof is universal for all finite transverse binary refinements. Standalone verifier independently evaluates all 256 patterns on 2x2x2 blocks and 565 heterogeneous feasible examples; finite experiments do not certify the theorem by themselves. Boundary all-singleton and one-doubleton cases checked.

value.rationale: The two-outcome common-refinement restriction is the first nontrivial departure from singleton cells in a natural exact-effectivity representation problem. The theorem classifies all per-block budgets at every finite parameter size, not an arbitrary numerical slice, and reduces exact minimum resource realization to a graph vertex cover with explicit attainable constructions. It separates genuinely needed duplication from excessive uniform padding and treats every feasible heterogeneous budget vector. This gives meaningful structural and quantitative content beyond proof correctness and novelty.
